202: /**
203:  * Pure management rules for the Dash Supplement Factory.
204:  *
205:  * The player takes empty pots from an unlimited intake, drags each one into the
206:  * station for its current numbered process, and moves it on before the ready
207:  * window expires. Stations process four pots at once. After all twelve
208:  * processes, a pot goes to the bottler and produces 20 one-second vials.
209:  *
210:  * The core has no DOM or wall clock. The host reports elapsed time with
211:  * `advance(deltaMs)` and receives every completion, spoil, and bottling event.
212:  */
213: export class DashSupplementFactory {
214:   constructor({ config = {} } = {}) {
215:     this.config = { ...DEFAULT_CONFIG, ...config };
216:     validateConfig(this.config);
217: 
218:     this.stations = this.config.stations.map((station) => ({ ...station }));
219:     this.processes = this.config.processes
220:       .map((process) => ({ ...process }))
221:       .sort((a, b) => a.order - b.order);
222: 
223:     this._pots = [];
224:     this._nextPotId = 1;
225:     this._elapsedMs = 0;
226:     this._vialsProduced = 0;
227:     this._potsBottled = 0;
228:     this._potsSpoiled = 0;
229:   }
230: 
231:   get pots() {
232:     return this._pots.map((pot) => ({ ...pot }));
233:   }
234: 
235:   get activePots() {
236:     return this._pots
237:       .filter((pot) => pot.location !== 'exited')
238:       .map((pot) => ({ ...pot }));
239:   }
240: 
241:   get intakePots() {
242:     return this.#potsAt('intake');
243:   }
244: 
245:   get elapsedMs() {
246:     return this._elapsedMs;
247:   }
248: 
249:   get vialsProduced() {
250:     return this._vialsProduced;
251:   }
252: 
253:   get secondsProduced() {
254:     return this._vialsProduced * this.config.secondsPerVial;
255:   }
256: 
257:   get potsBottled() {
258:     return this._potsBottled;
259:   }
260: 
261:   get potsSpoiled() {
262:     return this._potsSpoiled;
263:   }
264: 
265:   get stationCapacity() {
266:     return this.config.stationCapacity;
267:   }
268: 
269:   get bottlerCapacity() {
270:     return this.config.bottlerCapacity;
271:   }
272: 
273:   /** Active pots at one station, the intake, or the bottler. */
274:   getPotsAt(location) {
275:     return this.#potsAt(location);
276:   }
277: 
278:   /** Number of occupied slots per station, plus the bottler. */
279:   get occupancy() {
280:     const result = {};
281: 
282:     for (const station of this.stations) {
283:       result[station.id] = this.#potsAt(station.id).length;
284:     }
285:     result.bottler = this.#potsAt('bottler').length;
286: 
287:     return result;
288:   }
289: 
290:   /** The process that is running or awaiting movement for a pot, if any. */
291:   processFor(potId) {
292:     const pot = this._pots.find((candidate) => candidate.id === potId);
293: 
294:     if (!pot || pot.stepIndex >= this.processes.length) {
295:       return null;
296:     }
297:     return clone(this.processes[pot.stepIndex]);
298:   }
299: 
300:   /** Add one empty pot to the intake. There is no limit. */
301:   takePot() {
302:     const pot = {
303:       id: this._nextPotId,
304:       stepIndex: 0,
305:       location: 'intake',
306:       status: POT_STATUS.IDLE,
307:       progressMs: 0,
308:       windowMsLeft: 0,
309:       spoiled: false,
310:       bottled: false,
311:     };
312:     this._nextPotId += 1;
313:     this._pots.push(pot);
314: 
315:     return {
316:       type: 'pot-taken',
317:       potId: pot.id,
318:       pot: { ...pot },
319:       intake: this.#potsAt('intake').length,
320:     };
321:   }
322: 
323:   /**
324:    * Drag a pot into a station or the bottler.
325:    *
326:    * A pot waiting at the intake or ready at a station can move. Working pots
327:    * are rejected with `pot-busy`; a wrong station leaves the pot where it was.
328:    */
329:   dropPot(potId, targetId) {
330:     const pot = this._pots.find((candidate) => candidate.id === potId);
331: 
332:     if (!pot) {
333:       return this.#rejected('unknown-pot');
334:     }
335:     if (pot.location === 'exited' || pot.status === POT_STATUS.SPOILED) {
336:       return this.#rejected('pot-gone');
337:     }
338:     if (
339:       pot.status === POT_STATUS.WORKING ||
340:       pot.status === POT_STATUS.QUEUED ||
341:       pot.status === POT_STATUS.BOTTLING
342:     ) {
343:       return this.#rejected('pot-busy');
344:     }
345: 
346:     if (targetId === 'bottler') {
347:       return this.#dropAtBottler(pot);
348:     }
349: 
350:     const station = this.stations.find((candidate) => candidate.id === targetId);
351: 
352:     if (!station) {
353:       return this.#rejected('unknown-station');
354:     }
355:     if (pot.location === targetId) {
356:       return this.#rejected('already-there');
357:     }
358: 
359:     const step = this.processes[pot.stepIndex];
360: 
361:     if (!step) {
362:       return this.#rejected('ready-for-bottler');
363:     }
364:     if (step.stationId !== targetId) {
365:       return this.#rejected('wrong-station', {
366:         expectedStationId: step.stationId,
367:         process: clone(step),
368:       });
369:     }
370:     if (this.#potsAt(targetId).length >= this.config.stationCapacity) {
371:       return this.#rejected('station-full');
372:     }
373: 
374:     const from = pot.location;
375:     pot.location = targetId;
376:     pot.status = POT_STATUS.WORKING;
377:     pot.progressMs = 0;
378:     pot.windowMsLeft = 0;
379: 
380:     return {
381:       type: 'pot-dropped',
382:       potId: pot.id,
383:       from,
384:       to: targetId,
385:       status: pot.status,
386:       stepIndex: pot.stepIndex,
387:       step: clone(step),
388:     };
389:   }
390: 
391:   /**
392:    * Advance every working, ready, and bottling pot by `deltaMs`.
393:    *
394:    * Returns a tick with an ordered `events` array. The array can contain
395:    * process completions, spoiled pots, and bottled pots in the same tick.
396:    */
397:   advance(deltaMs) {
398:     if (!Number.isFinite(deltaMs) || deltaMs <= 0) {
399:       return this.#tick(0, []);
400:     }
401: 
402:     this._elapsedMs += deltaMs;
403:     const events = [];
404: 
405:     for (const pot of this._pots) {
406:       if (pot.status === POT_STATUS.WORKING) {
407:         const step = this.processes[pot.stepIndex];
408: 
409:         if (!step) {
410:           continue;
411:         }
412: 
413:         const completedIndex = pot.stepIndex;
414:         pot.progressMs += deltaMs;
415: 
416:         if (pot.progressMs >= step.durationMs) {
417:           const overflow = pot.progressMs - step.durationMs;
418:           pot.progressMs = step.durationMs;
419:           pot.status = POT_STATUS.READY;
420:           pot.windowMsLeft = step.windowMs;
421:           pot.stepIndex += 1;
422:           events.push({
423:             type: 'process-complete',
424:             potId: pot.id,
425:             stationId: pot.location,
426:             stepIndex: completedIndex,
427:             step: clone(step),
428:             nextStep: clone(this.processes[pot.stepIndex] ?? null),
429:             windowMsLeft: pot.windowMsLeft,
430:           });
431: 
432:           if (overflow > 0) {
433:             pot.windowMsLeft -= overflow;
434: 
435:             if (pot.windowMsLeft <= 0) {
436:               this.#spoil(pot, events, completedIndex);
437:             }
438:           }
439:         }
440:       } else if (pot.status === POT_STATUS.READY) {
441:         pot.windowMsLeft -= deltaMs;
442: 
443:         if (pot.windowMsLeft <= 0) {
444:           this.#spoil(pot, events, Math.max(0, pot.stepIndex - 1));
445:         }
446:       }
447:     }
448: 
449:     // The bottler empties one pot at a time. Anything else in the bottler
450:     // waits as a queue, so a large delta can finish several pots in order.
451:     let bottlingRemaining = deltaMs;
452: 
453:     while (bottlingRemaining > 0) {
454:       const active = this._pots.find(
455:         (candidate) =>
456:           candidate.location === 'bottler' &&
457:           candidate.status === POT_STATUS.BOTTLING,
458:       );
459: 
460:       if (!active) {
461:         break;
462:       }
463: 
464:       const needed = this.config.bottlingMs - active.progressMs;
465: 
466:       if (bottlingRemaining < needed) {
467:         active.progressMs += bottlingRemaining;
468:         break;
469:       }
470: 
471:       bottlingRemaining -= needed;
472:       active.progressMs = this.config.bottlingMs;
473:       active.status = POT_STATUS.DONE;
474:       active.bottled = true;
475:       active.location = 'exited';
476:       this._vialsProduced += this.config.vialsPerPot;
477:       this._potsBottled += 1;
478:       events.push({
479:         type: 'pot-bottled',
480:         potId: active.id,
481:         vials: this.config.vialsPerPot,
482:         seconds: this.config.vialsPerPot * this.config.secondsPerVial,
483:         vialsProduced: this._vialsProduced,
484:         secondsProduced: this.secondsProduced,
485:       });
486: 
487:       this.#promoteQueuedPot(events);
488:     }
489: 
490:     return this.#tick(deltaMs, events);
491:   }
492: 
493:   /** Remove all produced vials from the module and return the count. */
494:   takeVials() {
495:     const vials = this._vialsProduced;
496:     this._vialsProduced = 0;
497:     return vials;
498:   }
499: 
500:   /** Remove all produced vials and return their total speed duration. */
501:   takeSeconds() {
502:     return this.takeVials() * this.config.secondsPerVial;
503:   }
504: 
505:   /** Backwards-compatible aliases for hosts that still call them bottles. */
506:   takeBottles() {
507:     return this.takeVials();
508:   }
509: 
510:   #dropAtBottler(pot) {
511:     if (pot.stepIndex < this.processes.length) {
512:       return this.#rejected('processes-remaining', {
513:         process: clone(this.processes[pot.stepIndex]),
514:       });
515:     }
516:     if (this.#potsAt('bottler').length >= this.config.bottlerCapacity) {
517:       return this.#rejected('bottler-full');
518:     }
519: 
520:     const from = pot.location;
521:     const bottlerBusy = this._pots.some(
522:       (candidate) =>
523:         candidate.location === 'bottler' &&
524:         candidate.status === POT_STATUS.BOTTLING,
525:     );
526: 
527:     pot.location = 'bottler';
528:     pot.status = bottlerBusy ? POT_STATUS.QUEUED : POT_STATUS.BOTTLING;
529:     pot.progressMs = 0;
530:     pot.windowMsLeft = 0;
531: 
532:     return {
533:       type: 'pot-dropped',
534:       potId: pot.id,
535:       from,
536:       to: 'bottler',
537:       status: pot.status,
538:       stepIndex: pot.stepIndex,
539:       step: null,
540:     };
541:   }
542: 
543:   /** Start the next waiting pot in the bottler, if any. */
544:   #promoteQueuedPot(events) {
545:     const next = this._pots.find(
546:       (candidate) =>
547:         candidate.location === 'bottler' &&
548:         candidate.status === POT_STATUS.QUEUED,
549:     );
550: 
551:     if (!next) {
552:       return null;
553:     }
554: 
555:     next.status = POT_STATUS.BOTTLING;
556:     next.progressMs = 0;
557:     events.push({
558:       type: 'bottling-started',
559:       potId: next.id,
560:     });
561: 
562:     return next;
563:   }
564: 
565:   #spoil(pot, events, stepIndex = pot.stepIndex) {
566:     const stationId = pot.location;
567: 
568:     pot.status = POT_STATUS.SPOILED;
569:     pot.location = 'exited';
570:     pot.spoiled = true;
571:     pot.windowMsLeft = 0;
572:     pot.progressMs = 0;
573:     this._potsSpoiled += 1;
574:     events.push({
575:       type: 'pot-spoiled',
576:       potId: pot.id,
577:       stationId,
578:       stepIndex,
579:       reason: 'window',
580:     });
581:   }
582: 
583:   #potsAt(location) {
584:     return this._pots
585:       .filter((pot) => pot.location === location)
586:       .map((pot) => ({ ...pot }));
587:   }
588: 
589:   #tick(deltaMs, events) {
590:     return {
591:       type: 'tick',
592:       deltaMs,
593:       elapsedMs: this._elapsedMs,
594:       events,
595:       activePots: this._pots.filter((pot) => pot.location !== 'exited').length,
596:       vialsProduced: this._vialsProduced,
597:     };
598:   }

600:   #rejected(reason, extra = {}) {

602:       type: 'rejected',

## Assistant

Fixed the remaining Dash Supplement Factory failure.

**Cause:** the test had the fifth pot waiting as `READY` with a 300 ms window while the bottler ran for 400 ms, so the pot spoiled before it could be re-offered. The bottler capacity check itself was working correctly.

**Fix:**
- `dash-supplement-factory/test/dashSupplementFactoryCore.test.js:308` — the capacity test now uses a 5000 ms ready window so the fifth pot survives while the bottler drains.
- `checklist.md` — added a verified item for the four-pot bottler capacity rule.

- Dash Supplement Factory: **23/23 tests pass**
- Soul Clicker: **21/21 tests pass**
- Bullet Press: **18/21 tests pass** — three pre-existing failures unrelated to this change (`a default magazine fills after 10 keys`, `slower magazines award lower whole multipliers`, `multiplier uses the average time across the magazine`)

In `#dropAtBottler`:
- after capacity check, from = pot.location; pot.location='bottler'; progress=0; window=0.

But careful: if active bottling pot exists, new pot queued. If no active (all queued? impossible because when one completes it promotes next within same tick), start.

Advance:
- Find the active bottling pot: `const active = this._pots.find(p => p.location==='bottler' && p.status===BOTTLING)`.
- If active, progress only it by deltaMs. On completion: award vials, status DONE, location EXITED, bottled true, potsBottled++, event pot-bottled. Then promote the next queued pot (oldest by id or array order): set status BOTTLING, progress 0, and push event `bottling-started` with potId. Also leftover overflow? For correctness with large delta, we could carry overflow to next pot. The previous implementation didn't cascade but sequential now should ideally use overflow across pots. Deterministic and nicer: loop with remaining delta:
```
let remaining = deltaMs;
while (remaining > 0) {
  const active = find active bottling;
  if (!active) break;
  const needed = bottlingMs - active.progressMs;
  if (remaining < needed) { active.progressMs += remaining; remaining = 0; break; }
  remaining -= needed;
  complete active...
  promote next...
}
```
But be careful events ordering with other station processing in same tick. Current loop iterates all pots; bottler handling separate. We can handle bottler after station loop using the while. Also if delta huge (e.g., advance(60000)) it completes all sequential pots; good deterministic.

554: /* ---------- Arrows ---------- */
555: 
556: function svgElement(name) {
557:   return document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', name);
558: }
559: 
560: function nodeRect(id, canvasRect) {
561:   const el = id === 'intake' ? ui.intake : stationViews.get(id)?.card;
562:   if (!el) {
563:     return null;
564:   }
565: 
566:   const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
567:   return {
568:     left: rect.left - canvasRect.left,
569:     top: rect.top - canvasRect.top,
570:     width: rect.width,
571:     height: rect.height,
572:   };
573: }
574: 
575: function centerOf(rect) {
576:   return {
577:     x: rect.left + rect.width / 2,
578:     y: rect.top + rect.height / 2,
579:   };
580: }
581: 
582: function edgePoint(rect, toward, pad = 7) {
583:   const center = centerOf(rect);
584:   const dx = toward.x - center.x;
585:   const dy = toward.y - center.y;
586:   const halfW = rect.width / 2 + pad;
587:   const halfH = rect.height / 2 + pad;
588: 
589:   if (dx === 0 && dy === 0) {
590:     return center;
591:   }
592: 
593:   const scaleX = dx === 0 ? Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY : halfW / Math.abs(dx);
594:   const scaleY = dy === 0 ? Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY : halfH / Math.abs(dy);
595:   const scale = Math.min(scaleX, scaleY);
596: 
597:   return {
598:     x: center.x + dx * scale,
599:     y: center.y + dy * scale,
600:   };
601: }
602: 
603: function renderArrows() {
604:   const canvasRect = ui.canvas.getBoundingClientRect();
605:   const width = Math.max(1, Math.round(canvasRect.width));
606:   const height = Math.max(1, Math.round(canvasRect.height));
607: 
608:   ui.arrows.setAttribute('viewBox', `0 0 ${width} ${height}`);
609:   ui.arrows.replaceChildren();
610: 
611:   const defs = svgElement('defs');
612:   defs.innerHTML = `
613:     <marker id="arrow-dim" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="8" refY="5"
614:       markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" orient="auto-start-reverse">
615:       <path d="M0 0 10 5 0 10z" fill="#6d6855"></path>
616:     </marker>
617:     <marker id="arrow-gold" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="8" refY="5"
618:       markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" orient="auto-start-reverse">
619:       <path d="M0 0 10 5 0 10z" fill="#f2c94c"></path>
620:     </marker>
621:   `;
622:   ui.arrows.append(defs);
623: 
624:   const groups = new Map();
625: 
626:   for (const pot of core.activePots) {
627:     const destination = nextDestination(pot);
628:     if (!destination || destination.toId === pot.location) {
629:       continue;
630:     }
631: 
632:     const key = `${pot.location}->${destination.toId}`;
633:     let group = groups.get(key);
634: 
635:     if (!group) {
636:       group = {
637:         fromId: pot.location,
638:         toId: destination.toId,
639:         orders: new Set(),
640:         ready: false,
641:         count: 0,
642:       };
643:       groups.set(key, group);
644:     }
645: 
646:     group.count += 1;
647:     group.ready =
648:       group.ready ||
649:       pot.status === POT_STATUS.READY ||
650:       pot.location === 'intake';
651:     group.orders.add(destination.process?.order ?? 'BTL');
652:   }
653: 
654:   if (groups.size === 0 && core.activePots.length === 0) {
655:     groups.set('intake->mill', {
656:       fromId: 'intake',
657:       toId: 'mill',
658:       orders: new Set([1]),
659:       ready: false,
660:       count: 0,
661:     });
662:   }
663: 
664:   for (const group of groups.values()) {
665:     const fromRect = nodeRect(group.fromId, canvasRect);
666:     const toRect = nodeRect(group.toId, canvasRect);
667: 
668:     if (!fromRect || !toRect) {
669:       continue;
670:     }
671: 
672:     const start = edgePoint(fromRect, centerOf(toRect));
673:     const end = edgePoint(toRect, centerOf(fromRect));
674:     const dx = end.x - start.x;
675:     const dy = end.y - start.y;
676:     const distance = Math.hypot(dx, dy) || 1;
677:     const fromIndex = FLOW_INDEX[group.fromId] ?? 0;
678:     const toIndex = FLOW_INDEX[group.toId] ?? 0;
679:     const direction = fromIndex <= toIndex ? 1 : -1;
680:     const bend = Math.min(54, distance * 0.15) * direction;
681:     const normalX = -dy / distance;
682:     const normalY = dx / distance;
683:     const controlX = (start.x + end.x) / 2 + normalX * bend;
684:     const controlY = (start.y + end.y) / 2 + normalY * bend;
685: 
686:     const path = svgElement('path');
687:     path.setAttribute(
688:       'd',
689:       `M ${start.x} ${start.y} Q ${controlX} ${controlY} ${end.x} ${end.y}`,
690:     );
691:     path.setAttribute(
692:       'class',
693:       `arrow ${group.ready ? 'arrow--ready' : 'arrow--waiting'}`,
694:     );
695:     path.setAttribute(
696:       'marker-end',
697:       group.ready ? 'url(#arrow-gold)' : 'url(#arrow-dim)',
698:     );
699:     ui.arrows.append(path);
700: 
701:     const label = svgElement('text');
702:     label.setAttribute('x', String(0.25 * start.x + 0.5 * controlX + 0.25 * end.x));
703:     label.setAttribute('y', String(0.25 * start.y + 0.5 * controlY + 0.25 * end.y));
704:     label.setAttribute('text-anchor', 'middle');
705:     label.setAttribute('dominant-baseline', 'middle');
706:     label.setAttribute(
707:       'class',
708:       `arrow__label${group.ready ? ' arrow__label--ready' : ''}`,
709:     );
710:     label.textContent = [...group.orders].join('·');
711:     ui.arrows.append(label);
712:   }
713: }

20: Then open <http://localhost:8002/>.
21: 
22: ## Controls
23: 
24: | Action | Input |
25: | --- | --- |
26: | Collect an empty pot | `TAKE POT` in the top-left intake (no limit) |
27: | Move a pot | Drag it from the intake or a station and drop it on a station |
28: | Start a process | Drop a ready pot on the station for its current numbered process |
29: | Finish a pot | After process 12, drag it into the bottom-right bottler |
30: | Bank output | Vials leave the bottler automatically; `DASH` tracks seconds |
31: 
32: Stations process pots automatically. A pot turns **ready** when its process finishes, then a timer starts. Drag it to the next station before the timer empties or it spoils and is lost.
33: 
34: ## Floor
35: 
36: - **Intake** — top left, unlimited empty pots.
37: - **Six stations** — grain mill, mash vat, agitator press, spirit still, purity filter, and plan bureau. Every station has a 2×2 grid of four slots plus a machine protrusion.
38: - **Bottler** — bottom right. Four slots. Vials stream off the right edge; emptied pots fall off the bottom edge.
39: - **Info panel** — bottom left. Title, live stats, all twelve numbered processes, and the current hint.
40: - **Arrows** — drawn from each pot's station to its next required station, labelled with the process number. Bright gold arrows are ready to follow; dashed arrows are still processing.
41: 
42: ## Process plan
43: 
44: | # | Process | Station | Work | Window |
45: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
46: | 1 | Seize the Harvest | Mill | 1500 ms | 7000 ms |
47: | 2 | Nationalize the Mash | Vat | 1400 ms | 7000 ms |
48: | 3 | Agitate the Masses | Press | 1200 ms | 6500 ms |
49: | 4 | Distill the Spirit | Still | 1900 ms | 6500 ms |
50: | 5 | Collectivize the Vat | Vat | 1500 ms | 7000 ms |
51: | 6 | Purge Deviations | Filter | 1400 ms | 6500 ms |
52: | 7 | Ratify the Plan | Bureau | 1200 ms | 7000 ms |
53: | 8 | Five-Year Ferment | Still | 2100 ms | 6500 ms |
54: | 9 | Commissar's Blend | Vat | 1500 ms | 7000 ms |
55: | 10 | Inspect the Cadre | Bureau | 1300 ms | 6500 ms |
56: | 11 | Filter the Line | Filter | 1700 ms | 6500 ms |
57: | 12 | Seal the Revolution | Press | 1400 ms | 7000 ms |
58: 
59: The vat is used three times; the still, filter, bureau, and press twice; the mill once. The bottler is the final destination.
60: 
61: ## Rules implemented
62: 
63: - The intake has no pot limit; `TAKE POT` always works.
64: - Each station holds four pots at once. A fifth drop is rejected and stays in its source.
65: - A pot can only enter the station required by its current process. A wrong station is rejected; the pot stays where it was.
66: - Stations process automatically. A working pot cannot be picked up.
67: - When work finishes the pot becomes ready and a window timer starts.
68: - If the window expires, the pot spoils, leaves the station, and frees its slot.
69: - After process 12, the pot can enter the bottler. Earlier drops are rejected.
70: - The bottler holds four pots and empties each pot over ten seconds (`bottlingMs`). The pot's liquid level visibly drains while it bottles.
71: - Each pot yields 20 vials; each vial is 1 second of dash.
72: - Vials are awarded when bottling finishes. The emptied pot leaves the floor.
73: - The core is deterministic and replayable from the same action sequence. The browser passes frame deltas to `advance()`.
74: 
75: ## Core API
76: 
77: ```js
78: import {
79:   DashSupplementFactory,
80:   POT_STATUS,
81:   PROCESSES,
82:   STATIONS,
83: } from './src/dashSupplementFactoryCore.js';
84: 
85: const factory = new DashSupplementFactory();
86: 
87: factory.takePot();                    // unlimited intake pot
88: factory.dropPot(1, 'mill');           // starts process 1
89: factory.advance(1500);                // tick: returns process-complete
90: factory.dropPot(1, 'vat');            // starts process 2
91: factory.advance(1400);
92: // ...continue through the plan...
93: factory.dropPot(1, 'bottler');        // only after process 12
94: factory.advance(10000);               // tick: returns pot-bottled
95: factory.takeVials();                  // 20, then resets
96: factory.takeSeconds();                // 20, then resets
97: ```
98: 
99: Useful getters: `processes`, `stations`, `pots`, `activePots`, `intakePots`, `occupancy`, `vialsProduced`, `secondsProduced`, `potsBottled`, `potsSpoiled`, `elapsedMs`, `stationCapacity`, and `bottlerCapacity`.
100: 
101: `dropPot()` returns `pot-dropped` or `rejected` with a reason such as `wrong-station`, `station-full`, `bottler-full`, `pot-busy`, `processes-remaining`, or `pot-gone`.
102: 
103: `advance(deltaMs)` returns `{ type: 'tick', events, elapsedMs, ... }`. Events can include `process-complete`, `pot-spoiled`, and `pot-bottled` in the same tick.
104: 
105: ## Configuration
106: 
107: | Option | Default | Meaning |
108: | --- | --- | --- |
109: | `stations` | `STATIONS` | Six station definitions |

165: - Process 12 must finish before the bottler accepts the pot.
166: - The bottler holds four pots and empties each pot over `10000 ms`; the pot's liquid drains visibly while it bottles.
167: - One pot produces 20 vials; one vial is one second of dash.
168: - Vials are only awarded when bottling finishes.
169: - The core is deterministic and replayable; the browser owns the clock and reports deltas.
170: 
171: Core interface:
172: 
173: - Mutations: `takePot()`, `dropPot(potId, targetId)`, `advance(deltaMs)`.
174: - Output: `takeVials()`, `takeSeconds()`, `takeBottles()` alias.
175: - State: `processes`, `stations`, `pots`, `activePots`, `intakePots`, `occupancy`, `vialsProduced`, `secondsProduced`, `potsBottled`, `potsSpoiled`, `elapsedMs`, `stationCapacity`, `bottlerCapacity`.
176: - `dropPot()` returns `pot-dropped` or `rejected` (`wrong-station`, `station-full`, `bottler-full`, `pot-busy`, `processes-remaining`, `pot-gone`).
177: - `advance()` returns a tick with ordered `events` (`process-complete`, `pot-spoiled`, `pot-bottled`).
178: 
179: Browser shell as built:
180: 
181: - Separate station cards, no belt. Each card has a machine protrusion and four slots.
182: - Pointer drag-and-drop from the intake or a ready station to the next station or bottler.
183: - Gold arrows show the next hop for ready pots; dashed arrows show the hop still processing.
184: - The bottom-left panel shows title, IN PLAY / VIALS / DASH / SPOILED, all twelve numbered processes, and a live hint.
185: - Pots show a process badge, fill level, work progress, and a ready-window timer.
186: - Bottling takes ten seconds per pot and drains its liquid visibly, then streams vial sprites off the right edge; emptied pots fall off the bottom edge.
187: - Wrong drops raise a toast; spoiled pots are removed and counted.
188: - The line never ends or batches; play continues as long as the player takes pots.

46914:  "newString": "Purpose: a station-management factory game that produces dash seconds.\n\nImplemented: `dash-supplement-factory/src/dashSupplementFactoryCore.js` (pure rules, no DOM or wall-clock), `test/dashSupplementFactoryCore.test.js` (21 tests), and a browser shell in `dash-supplement-factory/` (`index.html`, `styles.css`, `src/main.js`, `src/assets.js`, `assets/bottle.svg`, `assets/vial.svg`). Run it with `python3 -m http.server 8002` from the module folder.\n\nFlow:\n\n1. Take unlimited empty pots from the top-left intake.\n2. Drag each pot into the station for its current numbered process.\n3. The station processes automatically. Move the pot before its ready window expires.\n4. Repeat through twelve processes over six reusable stations.\n5. After process 12, drag the pot into the bottom-right bottler.\n6. Bottling produces 20 vials of one-second dash; vials leave right, emptied pots leave bottom.\n\nLayout:\n\n- Intake top left.\n- Six separate stations with 2×2 slot grids and machine protrusions: mill, vat, press, still, filter, bureau.\n- Bottler bottom right.\n- Info panel bottom left with title, live stats, the full numbered process plan, and the current hint.\n- Dynamic route arrows run from each pot's station to its next required station and are labelled with the process number.\n\nProcesses as implemented:\n\n| # | Process | Station | Work | Window |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| 1 | Seize the Harvest | Mill | 1500 ms | 7000 ms |\n| 2 | Nationalize the Mash | Vat | 1400 ms | 7000 ms |\n| 3 | Agitate the Masses | Press | 1200 ms | 6500 ms |\n| 4 | Distill the Spirit | Still | 1900 ms | 6500 ms |\n| 5 | Collectivize the Vat | Vat | 1500 ms | 7000 ms |\n| 6 | Purge Deviations | Filter | 1400 ms | 6500 ms |\n| 7 | Ratify the Plan | Bureau | 1200 ms | 7000 ms |\n| 8 | Five-Year Ferment | Still | 2100 ms | 6500 ms |\n| 9 | Commissar's Blend | Vat | 1500 ms | 7000 ms |\n| 10 | Inspect the Cadre | Bureau | 1300 ms | 6500 ms |\n| 11 | Filter the Line | Filter | 1700 ms | 6500 ms |\n| 12 | Seal the Revolution | Press | 1400 ms | 7000 ms |\n\nThe vat is used three times; the still, filter, bureau, and press twice; the mill once.\n\nRules as implemented:\n\n- The intake is unlimited.\n- Each station holds four pots in a 2×2 grid. A fifth drop is rejected and stays at its source.\n- A pot can only enter the station for its current process. Wrong-station drops are rejected without losing the pot.\n- Stations process automatically; a working pot cannot leave.\n- A finished process opens a ready window. If the window empties, the pot spoils, leaves the station, and frees its slot.\n- Process 12 must finish before the bottler accepts the pot.\n- The bottler holds four pots and bottles one pot every `900 ms`.\n- One pot produces 20 vials; one vial is one second of dash.\n- Vials are only awarded when bottling finishes.\n- The core is deterministic and replayable; the browser owns the clock and reports deltas.\n\nCore interface:\n\n- Mutations: `takePot()`, `dropPot(potId, targetId)`, `advance(deltaMs)`.\n- Output: `takeVials()`, `takeSeconds()`, `takeBottles()` alias.\n- State: `processes`, `stations`, `pots`, `activePots`, `intakePots`, `occupancy`, `vialsProduced`, `secondsProduced`, `potsBottled`, `potsSpoiled`, `elapsedMs`, `stationCapacity`, `bottlerCapacity`.\n- `dropPot()` returns `pot-dropped` or `rejected` (`wrong-station`, `station-full`, `bottler-full`, `pot-busy`, `processes-remaining`, `pot-gone`).\n- `advance()` returns a tick with ordered `events` (`process-complete`, `pot-spoiled`, `pot-bottled`).\n\nBrowser shell as built:\n\n- Separate station cards, no belt. Each card has a machine protrusion and four slots.\n- Pointer drag-and-drop from the intake or a ready station to the next station or bottler.\n- Gold arrows show the next hop for ready pots; dashed arrows show the hop still processing.\n- The bottom-left panel shows title, IN PLAY / VIALS / DASH / SPOILED, all twelve numbered processes, and a live hint.\n- Pots show a process badge, fill level, work progress, and a ready-window timer.\n- Bottling streams vial sprites off the right edge; emptied pots fall off the bottom edge.\n- Wrong drops raise a toast; spoiled pots are removed and counted.\n- The line never ends or batches; play continues as long as the player takes pots.\n\nOpen questions:\n\n- Confirm one pot should yield 20 one-second vials.\n- Tune the process durations and ready windows through playtesting.\n- Confirm wrong-station drops should be free rather than spoiling or delaying the pot.\n- Decide whether the six-station, twelve-process plan is the final route.\n- Integrate `takeVials()` / `takeSeconds()` with the host speed resource.",

'/tmp/opencode/dash-layout.png';\nconst sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));\n\nconst server = spawn('python3', ['-m', 'http.server', '8002'], {\n  cwd: '/home/rabamari/Projects/netshoot/dash-supplement-factory',\n  stdio: 'ignore',\n});\nconst chrome = spawn(\n  '/opt/google/chrome/chrome',\n  [\n    '--headless=new',\n    '--no-sandbox',\n    '--disable-gpu',\n    '--hide-scrollbars',\n    '--mute-audio',\n    `--window-size=${WIDTH},${HEIGHT}`,\n    '--remote-debugging-port=9234',\n    '--user-data-dir=/tmp/opencode/chrome-dash-layout',\n    BASE,\n  ],\n  { stdio: 'ignore' },\n);\n\nlet ws;\ntry {\n  let target;\n  for (let i = 0; i < 80 && !target; i += 1) {\n    try {\n      const res = await fetch(`${DEBUG}/json/list`);\n      const list = await res.json();\n      target = list.find((t) => t.type === 'page' && t.url.startsWith(BASE));\n    } catch {}\n    if (!target) await sleep(150);\n  }\n  if (!target) throw new Error('no target');\n\n  ws = new WebSocket(target.webSocketDebuggerUrl);\n  await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {\n    ws.addEventListener('open', resolve, { once: true });\n    ws.addEventListener('error', reject, { once: true });\n  });\n\n  let id = 0;\n  const pending = new Map();\n  ws.addEventListener('message', (event) => {\n    const msg = JSON.parse(event.data);\n    if (msg.id && pending.has(msg.id)) {\n      const { resolve, reject } = pending.get(msg.id);\n      pending.delete(msg.id);\n      if (msg.error) reject(new Error(JSON.stringify(msg.error)));\n      else resolve(msg.result);\n    }\n  });\n  const send = (method, params = {}) =>\n    new Promise((resolve, reject) => {\n      const next = ++id;\n      pending.set(next, { resolve, reject });\n      ws.send(JSON.stringify({ id: next, method, params }));\n    });\n  const evaluate = async (expression) => {\n    const result = await send('Runtime.evaluate', {\n      expression,\n      awaitPromise: true,\n      returnByValue: true,\n    });\n    if (result.exceptionDetails) throw new Error(result.exceptionDetails.text);\n    return result.result.value;\n  };\n\n  await send('Runtime.enable');\n  await send('Page.enable');\n  await sleep(600);\n\n  await evaluate('for (let i = 0; i < 3; i += 1) document.getElementById(\"take-pot\").click()');\n  await evaluate('document.querySelector(\\'#action-panel [data-step-id=\"vodka\"]\\').click()');\n  await evaluate('document.querySelector(\\'#action-panel [data-step-id=\"beet-extract\"]\\').click()');\n  await sleep(300);\n\n  const metrics = await evaluate(`({\n    scrollWidth: document.documentElement.scrollWidth,\n    innerWidth: window.innerWidth,\n    scrollHeight: document.documentElement.scrollHeight,\n    innerHeight: window.innerHeight,\n  })`);\n  console.log(JSON.stringify(metrics));\n\n  const shot = await send('Page.captureScreenshot', { format: 'png' });\n  writeFileSync(OUT, Buffer.from(shot.data, 'base64'));\n  console.log(`saved ${OUT}`);\n} finally {\n  ws?.close();\n  chrome.kill('SIGKILL');\n  server.kill('SIGKILL');\n}\n",

1: # commieD-Idea
2: 
3: - Multiplayer maze shooter (browser-based)
4: - Large scale: 1000s of concurrent players across 200 cities globally
5: - Goal: be the last team standing
6: -the entire game is minimal in design and assets with the theme of communism(cause commieD=comm(unist)i(com)eD(y))
7: - Teams are divided uniformly.
8: - Teams share everything(from ammo, dashes, and even HP)
9: - If the team HP goes to 0, the entire team dies.
10: - on a team dying, only the n/2 best players will be revived with team hp also getting halved(number of plrs\*hp per players= team HP, simpool)
11: - dead players(the n/2 not selected to play), act as ghosts, who search and collect resources for the team.
12: - on the number of players in team reaching one, the team dies. and is eliminated.
13: 04 — ghost mode
14: - the ghosts will play minigames to earn resources 
15:      a clicker game where you need to "CONTRIBUTE" your soul to your comrades(communist game intensifies). To create 
16: 04 — Ghost Mode
17: - Players who aren't selected for revival become ghosts.
18: - Ghosts continue contributing to their team's survival.
19: - Ghosts can collect resources for their team.
20: - Ghosts can play minigames to generate resources.
21: - Different resource types have different minigames.
22: - Ghosts can choose which resource they want to contribute.
23: 05 — Soul Contribution
24: - Soul is a resource generated by ghosts.
25: - Souls are generated through a clicker minigame.
26: - Ghosts must click to contribute their souls to their comrades.
27: - Souls are converted into HP.
28: - Generated HP is added to the team's health pool.
29: - The required clicking rate is 5 CPS.
30: - At 5 CPS, a ghost generates 1 HP/s(stored, until needed by the live players)
31: - If the clicking rate falls below 5 CPS, HP is goes down by -0.2HP/s.
32: - Ghost-generated HP is used when living players have low health.
33: Health regeneration rules
34: - Teams without ghosts regenerate HP normally.
35: - Normal regeneration happens at a fixed rate.
36: - Normal regeneration does not happen instantly.
37: - Teams with ghosts cannot regenerate HP normally.
38: - Teams with ghosts depend on ghost-generated HP instead.
39: 06 — Bullet Press
40: -follow keyboard instructions to create magazines
41: -magazines can be rejected if the instructions followed are not perfect.
42: -the entire sequence must be completed for the next magazine manufacturing run.
43: -mistakes per magazine control a multiplier, if there are no magazine errors for a long time, the multiplier increases slwoly upto 5x. but reduces on tevery mistake till it is 0.5x production.
44: 07 — stewedluck:
45: -on every kill by the live players, the team gets killmit. which can be used to spin a stew pot to get any special powerup in the game.(communist engineering)

3: Status: Soul Clicker, Bullet Press, and Dash Supplement Factory are implemented under their own folders; Stewed Luck is not started. `idea.md` is still the product source of truth; this file records the working details and open questions for the ghost minigames.
4: 
5: ## Shared contract
6: 
7: - Minigames are self-contained modules: explicit state/input in, resources/events out.
8: - Do not own the main game loop, networking, or global game state.
9: - Rules must be deterministic and testable; avoid wall-clock time.
10: - Use dummy/placeholder assets everywhere for now; keep asset paths centralized.
11: 
12: ## 1. Soul Clicker (Soul Contribution)
13: 
14: Purpose: a ghost contributes their soul to increase the team's HP.
15: 
16: Implemented: `soul-clicker/` (ES modules, no dependencies). Tests run with `node --test`.
17: 
18: Rules as implemented:
19: 
20: - Click the central soul sprite to contribute.
21: - CPS is measured over a rolling 10-second window.
22: - At `CPS >= 5`: add HP at `0.2 × CPS` per second. At exactly 5 CPS this is the specified `+1 HP/s`.
23: - At `CPS < 5`: lose `0.2 HP/s` continuously.
24: - HP is settled immediately on every click (and every frame), so crossing 5 CPS switches from loss to gain at the click itself.
25: - Team HP has **no maximum cap**.
26: - HP bar spans half the screen at the top and shows the numeric HP.
27: - With `baseline = 100 × living teammates`, the bar is:
28:   - **red** when `hp < baseline`,
29:   - **yellow** when `baseline <= hp <= baseline + 90`,
30:   - **green** when `hp > baseline + 90`.
31: - The bar fill is scaled to `baseline + 90`, clamped at 100%; the numeric HP keeps growing beyond it.
32: - Random shapes appear every 10–30 seconds at random screen positions. Clicking one grants `+5 HP`; missing it has no penalty.
33: - Shape types: circle, square, triangle, diamond, star.
34: - Press **Q** to pause/resume. Pausing freezes HP gain/loss, the CPS window, and shape timers; pause duration is removed from game time.
35: - Visual effects and polish are deferred; the UI is intentionally minimal and uses placeholder assets (flat shapes, no fades, glows, or transitions).
36: 
37: Confirmed by user:
38: 
39: - Central clickable soul creates team HP.
40: - Revived teams with ghosts have no HP cap because they cannot regenerate.
41: - Red / yellow / green band thresholds above.
42: 
43: Assumed (change if wrong):
44: 
45: - HP gain keeps scaling above 5 CPS (`0.2 × CPS`) rather than capping at `1 HP/s`.
46: - Each collected shape gives `+5 HP`; missed shapes have no penalty.
47: - The minimum HP floor is `0`.
48: - Ghost stacking behaviour is deferred to the host game; the module tracks one ghost's contribution.
49: 
50: Open questions:
51: 
52: - Define the bank cap/decay once the host team economy exists.
53: - Define how multiple ghosts on one team stack.
54: - Confirm the `+5 HP` shape bonus and whether missing should hurt.
55: 
56: ## 2. Bullet Press
57: 
58: Purpose: ghosts produce magazines that living teammates load into their guns.
59: 
60: Implemented: `bullet-press/` (ES modules, no dependencies). Tests run with `node --test`.
61: 
62: Layout (top to bottom): sequence presenter → centered full-width magazine line → branch lines → single horizontal feeder. The current magazine sits at the center of the screen, with two empty magazines queued to its left and the previous magazine to its right. The feeder enters from the right and stops at the leftmost branch, so it serves only this station. It sits above the 10 branch layers. Ten vertical branch lines rise from it, one per slot, each carrying a column of bullets up to the magazine. The feeder is clogged while the branches are full: loading a slot pulls the top bullet from its branch into the magazine, refills that branch from the feeder, and indexes the feeder forward by exactly one bullet. Bullets and feed lines are centered on their slots. Magazine and sequence objects use a 5% larger scale.
63: 
64: Rules as implemented:
65: 
66: - One sequence fills one magazine. The sequence is 10 characters drawn from `A–Z`.
67: - The player types the sequence in order; lowercase input is accepted.
68: - A correct key pulls the top bullet from that slot's branch into the magazine, refills the branch from the feeder, indexes the feeder by one bullet, and fills the slot green.
69: - A wrong key pulls the top bullet in red, refills the branch, indexes the feeder, fills the slot red, and marks the whole magazine broken.
70: - A broken magazine **cannot be discarded immediately**. It stays until every slot is filled.
71: - When all slots are filled, the line shifts right: the current magazine becomes the previous one, a waiting magazine moves to the center, and a new empty magazine enters from the left. Older previous magazines slide farther right and fade out.
72: - A perfect magazine produces `multiplier` magazines.
73: - A broken magazine produces nothing and increments the broken count.
74: - The multiplier is a **whole number from 1 to 5**, based on average time per key across the completed magazine:
75:   - `≤ 400 ms/key` → `x5`
76:   - `≤ 600 ms/key` → `x4`
77:   - `≤ 800 ms/key` → `x3`
78:   - `≤ 1100 ms/key` → `x2`
79:   - slower → `x1`
80: - The timer starts when the magazine docks, not while it slides in.
81: - Production is an integer; `takeMagazines()` returns whole magazines to the host.
82: - Sequences come from a seeded RNG (or an injected RNG), never `Math.random()`.
83: 
84: Assumed (change if wrong):
85: 
86: - The sequence length and the number of magazine slots are the same value.
87: - Letters only (no digits or punctuation), to avoid confusion such as `0` vs `O`.
88: - Input is keyboard-only; no on-screen keypad yet.
89: - Speed is the only multiplier input; accuracy only decides perfect vs broken.
90: - A broken magazine awards `x0` because it produces nothing.
91: - The speed thresholds are placeholders for playtesting.
92: - No Q pause; `Q` is a valid sequence character.
93: 
94: Open questions:
95: 
96: - Tune the speed thresholds to the real feel of the game.
97: - Confirm that a broken magazine should award `x0` rather than a low whole multiplier.
98: - Confirm whether production should stay whole magazines in the host economy.
99: 
100: ## 3. Stewed Luck
101: 
102: Purpose: spend killmit earned by live-player kills to spin the communist stew pot for a special item/power-up.
103: 
104: Rules:
105: 
106: - Each live-player kill grants killmit to the team.
107: - Spend killmit to spin the pot.
108: - The spin returns a random special power-up.
109: - The pot is a "stewed luck" / communist pot edition wheel.
110: 
111: Open questions:
112: 
113: - Define the power-up list and spin weights.
114: - Define spin cost, duplicate handling, duration, and whether one player can spam spins.
115: 
116: ## 4. Dash Supplement Factory
117: 
118: Purpose: a station-management factory game that produces dash seconds.
119: 
120: Implemented: `dash-supplement-factory/src/dashSupplementFactoryCore.js` (pure rules, no DOM or wall-clock), `test/dashSupplementFactoryCore.test.js` (21 tests), and a browser shell in `dash-supplement-factory/` (`index.html`, `styles.css`, `src/main.js`, `src/assets.js`, `assets/bottle.svg`, `assets/vial.svg`). Run it with `python3 -m http.server 8002` from the module folder.
121: 
122: Flow:
123: 
124: 1. Take unlimited empty pots from the top-left intake.
125: 2. Drag each pot into the station for its current numbered process.
126: 3. The station processes automatically. Move the pot before its ready window expires.
127: 4. Repeat through twelve processes over six reusable stations.
128: 5. After process 12, drag the pot into the bottom-right bottler.
129: 6. Bottling produces 20 vials of one-second dash; vials leave right, emptied pots leave bottom.
130: 
131: Layout:
132: 
133: - Intake top left.
134: - Six separate stations with 2×2 slot grids and machine protrusions: mill, vat, press, still, filter, bureau.
135: - Bottler bottom right.
136: - Info panel bottom left with title, live stats, the full numbered process plan, and the current hint.
137: - Dynamic route arrows run from each pot's station to its next required station and are labelled with the process number.
138: 
139: Processes as implemented:
140: 
141: | # | Process | Station | Work | Window |
142: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
143: | 1 | Seize the Harvest | Mill | 1500 ms | 7000 ms |
144: | 2 | Nationalize the Mash | Vat | 1400 ms | 7000 ms |
145: | 3 | Agitate the Masses | Press | 1200 ms | 6500 ms |
146: | 4 | Distill the Spirit | Still | 1900 ms | 6500 ms |
147: | 5 | Collectivize the Vat | Vat | 1500 ms | 7000 ms |
148: | 6 | Purge Deviations | Filter | 1400 ms | 6500 ms |
149: | 7 | Ratify the Plan | Bureau | 1200 ms | 7000 ms |
150: | 8 | Five-Year Ferment | Still | 2100 ms | 6500 ms |
151: | 9 | Commissar's Blend | Vat | 1500 ms | 7000 ms |
152: | 10 | Inspect the Cadre | Bureau | 1300 ms | 6500 ms |
153: | 11 | Filter the Line | Filter | 1700 ms | 6500 ms |
154: | 12 | Seal the Revolution | Press | 1400 ms | 7000 ms |
155: 
156: The vat is used three times; the still, filter, bureau, and press twice; the mill once.
157: 
158: Rules as implemented:
159: 
160: - The intake is unlimited.
161: - Each station holds four pots in a 2×2 grid. A fifth drop is rejected and stays at its source.
162: - A pot can only enter the station for its current process. Wrong-station drops are rejected without losing the pot.
163: - Stations process automatically; a working pot cannot leave.
164: - A finished process opens a ready window. If the window empties, the pot spoils, leaves the station, and frees its slot.
165: - Process 12 must finish before the bottler accepts the pot.
166: - The bottler holds four pots and empties them one at a time over `10000 ms` each; waiting pots queue, and only the active pot's liquid drains visibly.
167: - One pot produces 20 vials; one vial is one second of dash.
168: - Vials are only awarded when bottling finishes. Vials appear one at a time during the drain and ride the upper outfeed belt; the emptied pot rides the lower belt away without fading.
169: - The core is deterministic and replayable; the browser owns the clock and reports deltas.
170: 
171: Core interface:
172: 
173: - Mutations: `takePot()`, `dropPot(potId, targetId)`, `advance(deltaMs)`.
174: - Output: `takeVials()`, `takeSeconds()`, `takeBottles()` alias.
175: - State: `processes`, `stations`, `pots`, `activePots`, `intakePots`, `occupancy`, `vialsProduced`, `secondsProduced`, `potsBottled`, `potsSpoiled`, `elapsedMs`, `stationCapacity`, `bottlerCapacity`.
176: - `dropPot()` returns `pot-dropped` or `rejected` (`wrong-station`, `station-full`, `bottler-full`, `pot-busy`, `processes-remaining`, `pot-gone`).
177: - `advance()` returns a tick with ordered `events` (`process-complete`, `pot-spoiled`, `pot-bottled`).
178: 
179: Browser shell as built:
180: 
181: - Separate station cards with no belt between stations. Each card has a machine protrusion and four slots. The bottler has two short outfeed belts: vials above, empties below.
182: - Pointer drag-and-drop from the intake or a ready station to the next station or bottler.
183: - Gold arrows show the next hop for ready pots; dashed arrows show the hop still processing.
184: - The bottom-left panel shows title, IN PLAY / VIALS / DASH / SPOILED, all twelve numbered processes, and a live hint.
185: - Pots show a process badge, fill level, work progress, and a ready-window timer.
186: - Bottling takes ten seconds per pot and drains its liquid visibly, then streams vial sprites off the right edge; emptied pots fall off the bottom edge.
187: - Wrong drops raise a toast; spoiled pots are removed and counted.
188: - The line never ends or batches; play continues as long as the player takes pots.
189: 
190: Open questions:
191: 
192: - Confirm one pot should yield 20 one-second vials.
193: - Tune the process durations and ready windows through playtesting.
194: - Confirm wrong-station drops should be free rather than spoiling or delaying the pot.
195: - Decide whether the six-station, twelve-process plan is the final route.
196: - Integrate `takeVials()` / `takeSeconds()` with the host speed resource.

2: 
3: A ghost minigame for **commieD**. Click your soul to contribute HP to the living teammates.
4:

8: - `src/clock.js` — pause-aware game clock; freezes time without shifting timestamps.
9: - `src/shapes.js` — random shape plans (type, position, size, delay, lifetime).
10: - `src/main.js` — browser wiring: HUD, soul clicks, shape spawning.

15: ## Rules implemented
16: 
17: - CPS is measured over a rolling 10-second window.

19: - Below 5 CPS, HP drops by `0.2 HP/s`.
20: - Team HP has **no maximum cap**.
21: - HP bar bands, with `baseline = 100 × living teammates`:
22:   - **red** below baseline,

70: ## Integration notes
71: 
72: - The core exposes `SoulClicker` with `click(nowMs)`, `advanceTo(nowMs)`, `tick(nowMs, deltaSeconds)`, `cpsAt(nowMs)`, `band`, `hp`, `baseline`, `fillRatio`, `addShapeBonus()`, and `setLivingTeammates(count)`.
73: - `click(nowMs)` settles the pending HP change immediately, then records the click. `advanceTo(nowMs)` does the same on every frame, so HP add/subtract follows the CPS counter without waiting.
74: - `nowMs` is host-supplied; rules never read the wall clock. The browser layer owns `performance.now()` and `requestAnimationFrame`.

1: # Bullet Press
2: 
3: A ghost minigame for **commieD**. One sequence fills one magazine. Type the displayed characters to pull bullets up into the magazine; wrong keys leave red slots. When every slot is filled, the magazine rolls out to the right and the next one enters from the left.
4: 
5: This module is self-contained:
6: 
7: - `src/bulletPressCore.js` — pure rules: sequences, slots, speed multiplier, production. No DOM or timers.
8: - `src/main.js` — browser wiring: keyboard input, assembly-line animation, bullet feeds, elapsed timer.
9: - `index.html` + `styles.css` — minimal placeholder UI. No image assets yet.
10: 
11: ## Layout
12: 
13: From top to bottom:
14: 
15: 1. **Sequence presenter** — the characters to type; the next one is highlighted. It sits above the magazine line.
16: 2. **Magazine line** — a full-width conveyor centered in the middle of the screen. The current 10-slot magazine sits on the line, with two empty magazines queued to its left and the previous magazine (if any) to its right.
17: 3. **Main feeder + branches** — a single horizontal bullet rail enters from the right and stops at the leftmost branch, so it only serves this station. Ten vertical feed lines branch upward from it, one per slot, each carrying a column of bullets. The rail sits above the branch layers and stays clogged while every branch is full. Loading a slot pulls its top bullet into the magazine and feeds a fresh bullet from the rail into the bottom of that branch, which indexes the rail forward by one bullet. A wrong key does the same and fills the line red.
18: 4. When all slots are filled, the line shifts right: the current magazine becomes the previous one, a waiting magazine slides into the center, and a fresh empty magazine enters from the left. Older previous magazines slide farther right and fade out.
19: 5. Magazine and sequence objects use a 5% larger scale than the base layout.
20: 
21: ## Rules implemented
22: 
23: - One sequence is 10 characters drawn from `A–Z`.
24: - A correct key fills the next magazine slot green, pulls that branch’s top bullet into the magazine, refills the bottom of that branch from the main feeder, indexes the feeder forward by one bullet, and fills the line upward.
25: - A wrong key fills the next slot red, pulls the top bullet in red, refills that branch from the feeder, indexes the feeder, and marks the whole magazine broken.
26: - A broken magazine **cannot be discarded immediately**. It stays until every slot is filled.
27: - Once all slots are filled, the magazine shifts right, becomes the previous magazine, and a waiting magazine moves into the center.
28: - A perfect magazine produces `multiplier` magazines.
29: - A broken magazine produces nothing and increments the broken count.
30: - The multiplier is a **whole number from 1 to 5**, based on typing speed across the completed magazine:
31: 
32: | Average time per key | Multiplier |
33: | -------------------- | ---------- |
34: | ≤ 400 ms             | x5         |
35: | ≤ 600 ms             | x4         |
36: | ≤ 800 ms             | x3         |
37: | ≤ 1100 ms            | x2         |
38: | slower               | x1         |
39: 
40: - A broken magazine awards `x0` because it produces nothing.
41: - Production is an integer; `takeMagazines()` returns the whole magazines produced and resets the counter.
42: - The timer starts when a magazine reaches the center (`start(nowMs)`), not while it is sliding in.
43: - Sequences come from a seeded RNG (or an injected RNG), never `Math.random()`.
44: - There is no Q pause; `Q` is a valid sequence character.
45: 
46: ## Controls
47: 
48: - Type the highlighted character with the keyboard.
49: - Letter keys only; digits, punctuation, and modifiers are ignored.
50: 
51: ## Run
52: 
53: ES modules need an HTTP server:
54: 
55: ```bash
56: cd bullet-press
57: python3 -m http.server 8001
58: ```
59: 
60: Open <http://localhost:8001/>.
61: 
62: ## Test
63: 
64: Uses Node's built-in test runner; no dependencies.
65: 
66: ```bash
67: cd bullet-press
68: npm test
69: ```
70: 
71: or directly:
72: 
73: ```bash
74: node --test
75: ```
76: 
77: ## Integration notes
78: 
79: - `BulletPress` exposes `sequence`, `slots`, `index`, `filled`, `complete`, `brokenMagazine`, `multiplierForDuration(durationMs)`, `lastMultiplier`, `lastDurationMs`, `production`, `magazinesProduced`, and `brokenMagazines`.
80: - `start(nowMs)` begins the current magazine’s timer once it is docked.
81: - `press(char, nowMs)` returns an event with `type` (`correct` / `wrong` / `ignored` / `not-ready`), `slotIndex`, `complete`, `broken`, `multiplier`, `durationMs`, and the current production.
82: - `nextMagazine(nowMs)` starts a fresh sequence only after the current magazine is complete. Omit `nowMs` and call `start(nowMs)` when the magazine docks.
83: - `takeMagazines()` is the resource-out call for the host game.
84: - Sequences are deterministic from a seed or an injected RNG.
85: 
86: ## Assumptions
87: 
88: - Letters only (no digits or punctuation), to avoid confusion such as `0` vs `O`.
89: - The sequence length and magazine slots are the same value (`sequenceLength`).
90: - Speed is the only multiplier input; accuracy only decides whether the magazine is perfect or broken.
91: - The speed thresholds are placeholders and should be tuned with playtesting.
92: - A broken magazine is counted once, when it finishes and is ejected.

+# commieD-Idea
+
+- Multiplayer maze shooter (browser-based)
+- Large scale: 1000s of concurrent players across 200 cities globally
+- Goal: be the last team standing
+-the entire game is minimal in design and assets with the theme of communism(cause commieD=comm(unist)i(com)eD(y))
+- Teams are divided uniformly.
+- Teams share everything(from ammo, dashes, and even HP)
+- If the team HP goes to 0, the entire team dies.
+- on a team dying, only the n/2 best players will be revived with team hp also getting halved(number of plrs\*hp per players= team HP, simpool)
+- dead players(the n/2 not selected to play), act as ghosts, who search and collect resources for the team.
+- on the number of players in team reaching one, the team dies. and is eliminated.
+04 — ghost mode
+- the ghosts will play minigames to earn resources 
+     a clicker game where you need to "CONTRIBUTE" your soul to your comrades(communist game intensifies). To create 
+04 — Ghost Mode
+- Players who aren't selected for revival become ghosts.
+- Ghosts continue contributing to their team's survival.
+- Ghosts can collect resources for their team.
+- Ghosts can play minigames to generate resources.
+- Different resource types have different minigames.
+- Ghosts can choose which resource they want to contribute.
+05 — Soul Contribution
+- Soul is a resource generated by ghosts through a clicker minigame.
+- Ghosts click the central soul sprite to contribute their souls to their comrades.
+- Souls are converted into HP and added to the team's health pool.
+- The clicking rate (CPS) is measured over a rolling 10-second window.
+- At 5 CPS or more, a ghost generates 0.2 × CPS HP/s; exactly 5 CPS is 1 HP/s.
+- Below 5 CPS, team HP drops by 0.2 HP/s.
+- Generated HP is banked until living players need it, with no maximum cap.
+- The HP bar is red below 100 × living teammates, yellow up to that baseline + 90, and green above.
+- Random shapes appear every 10–30 seconds; clicking one grants +5 HP.
+- Ghost-generated HP is used when living players have low health.
+- Q pauses and resumes the minigame.
+Health regeneration rules
+- Teams without ghosts regenerate HP normally.
+- Normal regeneration happens at a fixed rate.
+- Normal regeneration does not happen instantly.
+- Teams with ghosts cannot regenerate HP normally.
+- Teams with ghosts depend on ghost-generated HP instead.
+06 — Bullet Press
+- Follow keyboard instructions to create magazines.
+- One sequence fills one magazine; a sequence is 10 characters drawn from A–Z, typed in order.
+- A correct key fills the next slot green; a wrong key fills it red and marks the whole magazine broken.
+- A broken magazine cannot be discarded; it stays until all 10 slots are filled, then produces nothing.
+- The entire sequence must be completed for the next magazine run.
+- A perfect magazine produces magazines equal to the multiplier.
+- The multiplier is a whole number from 1x to 5x based on average time per key: ≤400 ms is x5, ≤600 ms x4, ≤800 ms x3, ≤1100 ms x2, slower x1.
+- A broken magazine awards x0 and increments the broken count.
+- Finished magazines eject to the right and the next empty magazine enters from the left.
+- takeMagazines() returns whole magazines to the team.
+07 — stewedluck:
+-on every kill by the live players, the team gets killmit. which can be used to spin a stew pot to get any special powerup in the game.(communist engineering)
+08-dash supplement factory
+- A station-management factory game that produces dash seconds.
+- Take empty pots from the unlimited intake and drag them through twelve numbered processes over six reusable stations.
+- Each station holds four pots in a 2×2 grid and processes automatically; a pot must be moved before its ready window expires or it spoils and frees its slot.
+- A pot can only enter the station for its current process; wrong-station drops are rejected for free.
+- Process 12 must finish before the bottler accepts the pot.
+- The bottler holds four pots and empties them one at a time over ten seconds each; waiting pots queue.
+- One pot produces 20 vials; one vial is one second of dash.
+- Vials ride the upper outfeed belt as the pot drains; the emptied pot rides the lower belt away.
+- takeVials() / takeSeconds() return the produced dash to the team.
\ No newline at end of file

1: # commieD-Idea
2: 
3: 01main requisites
4: - Multiplayer maze shooter (browser-based)
5: - Large scale: 1000s of concurrent players across 200 cities globally
6: - Goal: be the last team standing
7: - the entire game is minimal in design and assets with the theme of communism(cause commieD=comm(unist)i(com)eD(y))
8: - Teams are divided uniformly.
9: - Teams share everything(from ammo, dashes, and even HP)
10: - If the team HP goes to 0, the entire team dies.
11: - A team is revived with only n/2 of the number of players who were alive in the previous run.
12: - the players who get to live is decided by a random player in the team.
13: - dead players(the n/2 not selected to play), act as ghosts, who search and collect resources for the team.
14: - on the number of players in team reaching one, the team dies. and is eliminated.
15: 02actual gameplay
16: - the entire game happens in a limited procedurally generated maze.
17: - each team begins in a large empty space surrounded by the maze. which is its spawn point. enemies cannot enter here. and spawn vulnerability is also here. 
18: - the whole game is top down 2d.
19: - the screen will consist of the following:
20: .top left=minimap which will either show the nearby area, minimap of the whole maze or a list of your teammates which you can quickly select from by using arrow keys to get the route to them.(these different modes can be switched by using x key)
21: .top center=performance and connection stats. strip format. with colour change for good, acceptable and bad stat values.
22: .bottom left=team reserves(ammo, dash, current powerup)
23: .bottom center=team health
24: .top right=comrats(stats of your comrades)
25: - you move around with wasd and arrowkeys, shift to dash. mouse to aim and click to shoot. hold click to for continuous fire. space for using special item
26: - special items are found around the world as collectibles strewn around in mazes
27: - the maze itself is a tiled system containing the following types of tiles: wall, free space,. this is saved and used by program with the help of a 1d array whose scale is fixed at a square for now.
28: - for ghosts, they can immediately switch between different tasks by using 1,2,3(clicker,ammo,dash)
29: - special items that can be triggered with space are 1 time and everyone gets the special item. in case more are collected, they become the current special item and the item before it is saved and becomes current item again when special items is empty. anybody can use this item and exhaust it for the entire team.(communism at peak).
30: - special items cannot be stacked. one can only be triggered when there are no current effects. effects are applied teamwide when triggered.
31: -special items can randomly spawn on any free 
32: 03maze design:
33: - the maze is a structure with large spaces for the team spawn points.
34: - it will be a 3 pass system. first randomly set the spawn areas fo the different teams, then generate the maze then at last generate the special items.

1: # commieD-Idea
2: 
3: - Multiplayer maze shooter (browser-based)
4: - Large scale: 1000s of concurrent players across 200 cities globally
5: - Goal: be the last team standing
6: -the entire game is minimal in design and assets with the theme of communism(cause commieD=comm(unist)i(com)eD(y))
7: - Teams are divided uniformly.
8: - Teams share everything(from ammo, dashes, and even HP)
9: - If the team HP goes to 0, the entire team dies.
10: - on a team dying, only the n/2 best players will be revived with team hp also getting halved(number of plrs\*hp per players= team HP, simpool)
11: - dead players(the n/2 not selected to play), act as ghosts, who search and collect resources for the team.
12: - on the number of players in team reaching one, the team dies. and is eliminated.
13: 04 — ghost mode
14: - the ghosts will play minigames to earn resources 
15:      a clicker game where you need to "CONTRIBUTE" your soul to your comrades(communist game intensifies). To create 
16: 04 — Ghost Mode
17: - Players who aren't selected for revival become ghosts.
18: - Ghosts continue contributing to their team's survival.
19: - Ghosts can collect resources for their team.
20: - Ghosts can play minigames to generate resources.
21: - Different resource types have different minigames.
22: - Ghosts can choose which resource they want to contribute.
23: 05 — Soul Contribution
24: - Soul is a resource generated by ghosts through a clicker minigame.
25: - Ghosts click the central soul sprite to contribute their souls to their comrades.
26: - Souls are converted into HP and added to the team's health pool.
27: - The clicking rate (CPS) is measured over a rolling 10-second window.
28: - At 5 CPS or more, a ghost generates 0.2 × CPS HP/s; exactly 5 CPS is 1 HP/s.
29: - Below 5 CPS, team HP drops by 0.2 HP/s.
30: - Generated HP is banked until living players need it, with no maximum cap.
31: - The HP bar is red below 100 × living teammates, yellow up to that baseline + 90, and green above.
32: - Random shapes appear every 10–30 seconds; clicking one grants +5 HP.
33: - Ghost-generated HP is used when living players have low health.
34: - Q pauses and resumes the minigame.
35: Health regeneration rules
36: - Teams without ghosts regenerate HP normally.
37: - Normal regeneration happens at a fixed rate.
38: - Normal regeneration does not happen instantly.
39: - Teams with ghosts cannot regenerate HP normally.
40: - Teams with ghosts depend on ghost-generated HP instead.
41: 06 — Bullet Press
42: - Follow keyboard instructions to create magazines.
43: - One sequence fills one magazine; a sequence is 10 characters drawn from A–Z, typed in order.
44: - A correct key fills the next slot green; a wrong key fills it red and marks the whole magazine broken.
45: - A broken magazine cannot be discarded; it stays until all 10 slots are filled, then produces nothing.
46: - The entire sequence must be completed for the next magazine run.
47: - A perfect magazine produces magazines equal to the multiplier.
48: - The multiplier is a whole number from 1x to 5x based on average time per key: ≤400 ms is x5, ≤600 ms x4, ≤800 ms x3, ≤1100 ms x2, slower x1.
49: - A broken magazine awards x0 and increments the broken count.
50: - Finished magazines eject to the right and the next empty magazine enters from the left.
51: - takeMagazines() returns whole magazines to the team.
52: 07 --speed dash supplement factory:
53: - A station-management factory game that produces dash seconds.
54: - Take empty pots from the unlimited intake and drag them through twelve numbered processes over six reusable stations.
55: - Each station holds four pots in a 2×2 grid and processes automatically; a pot must be moved before its ready window expires or it spoils and frees its slot.
56: - A pot can only enter the station for its current process; wrong-station drops are rejected for free.
57: - Process 12 must finish before the bottler accepts the pot.
58: - The bottler holds four pots and empties them one at a time over ten seconds each; waiting pots queue.
59: - One pot produces 20 vials; one vial is one second of dash.
60: - Vials ride the upper outfeed belt as the pot drains; the emptied pot rides the lower belt away.
61: - takeVials() / takeSeconds() return the produced dash to the team.

## How to investigate

Read the highest-value sources first:
- `README*`, root manifests, workspace config, lockfiles
- build, test, lint, formatter, typecheck, and codegen config
- CI workflows and pre-commit / task runner config
- existing instruction files (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/rules/`, `.cursorrules`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`)
- repo-local OpenCode config such as `opencode.json`

If architecture is still unclear after reading config and docs, inspect a small number of representative code files to find the real entrypoints, package boundaries, and execution flow. Prefer reading the files that explain how the system is wired together over random leaf files.

Prefer executable sources of truth over prose. If docs conflict with config or scripts, trust the executable source and only keep what you can verify.

## What to extract

Look for the highest-signal facts for an agent working in this repo:
- exact developer commands, especially non-obvious ones
- how to run a single test, a single package, or a focused verification step
- required command order when it matters, such as `lint -> typecheck -> test`
- monorepo or multi-package boundaries, ownership of major directories, and the real app/library entrypoints
- framework or toolchain quirks: generated code, migrations, codegen, build artifacts, special env loading, dev servers, infra deploy flow
- testing quirks: fixtures, integration test prerequisites, snapshot workflows, required services, flaky or expensive suites
- important constraints from existing instruction files worth preserving

Good `AGENTS.md` content is usually hard-earned context that took reading multiple files to infer.

## Questions

Only ask the user questions if the repo cannot answer something important. Use the `question` tool for one short batch at most.

Good questions:
- undocumented team conventions
- branch / PR / release expectations
- missing setup or test prerequisites that are known but not written down

Do not ask about anything the repo already makes clear.

## Writing rules

Include only high-signal, repo-specific guidance such as:
- exact commands and shortcuts the agent would otherwise guess wrong
- architecture notes that are not obvious from filenames
- conventions that differ from language or framework defaults
- setup requirements, environment quirks, and operational gotchas
- references to existing instruction sources that matter

Exclude:
- generic software advice
- long tutorials or exhaustive file trees
- obvious language conventions
- speculative claims or anything you could not verify
- content better stored in another file referenced via `opencode.json` `instructions`

When in doubt, omit.

Prefer short sections and bullets. If the repo is simple, keep the file simple. If the repo is large, summarize the few structural facts that actually change how an agent should work.

If `AGENTS.md` already exists at `/home/rabamari/Projects/netshoot`, improve it in place rather than rewriting blindly. Preserve verified useful guidance, delete fluff or stale claims, and reconcile it with the current codebase.

1: # commieD-Idea
2: 
3: 01main requisites
4: - Multiplayer maze shooter (browser-based)
5: - Large scale: 1000s of concurrent players across 200 cities globally
6: - Goal: be the last team standing
7: - the entire game is minimal in design and assets with the theme of communism(cause commieD=comm(unist)i(com)eD(y))
8: - Teams are divided uniformly.
9: - Teams share everything(from ammo, dashes, and even HP)
10: - If the team HP goes to 0, the entire team dies.
11: - A team is revived with only n/2 of the number of players who were alive in the previous run.
12: - the players who get to live is decided by a random player in the team.
13: - dead players(the n/2 not selected to play), act as ghosts, who search and collect resources for the team.
14: - on the number of players in team reaching one, the team dies. and is eliminated.
15: 02actual gameplay
16: - the entire game happens in a limited procedurally generated maze.
17: - each team begins in a large empty space surrounded by the maze. which is its spawn point. enemies cannot enter here. and spawn vulnerability is also here. 
18: - the whole game is top down 2d.
19: - the screen will consist of the following:
20: .top left=minimap which will either show the nearby area, minimap of the whole maze or a list of your teammates which you can quickly select from by using arrow keys to get the route to them.(these different modes can be switched by using x key)
21: .top center=performance and connection stats. strip format. with colour change for good, acceptable and bad stat values.
22: .bottom left=team reserves(ammo, dash, current powerup)
23: .bottom center=team health
24: .top right=comrats(stats of your comrades)
25: - you move around with wasd and arrowkeys, shift to dash. mouse to aim and click to shoot. hold click to for continuous fire. space for using special item
26: - special items are found around the world as collectibles strewn around in mazes
27: - the maze itself is a tiled system containing the following types of tiles: wall, free space,. this is saved and used by program with the help of a 1d array whose scale is fixed at a square for now.
28: - for ghosts, they can immediately switch between different tasks by using 1,2,3(clicker,ammo,dash)
29: - special items that can be triggered with space are 1 time and everyone gets the special item. in case more are collected, they become the current special item and the item before it is saved and becomes current item again when special items is empty. anybody can use this item and exhaust it for the entire team.(communism at peak).
30: - special items cannot be stacked. one can only be triggered when there are no current effects. effects are applied teamwide when triggered.
31: -special items can randomly spawn on any free 
32: 03maze design:
33: - the maze is a structure with large spaces for the team spawn points.
34: - it will be a 3 pass system. first randomly set the spawn areas fo the different teams, then generate the maze then at last generate the special items.
35: - each tile is the same size as the player. the player is a circle with 1 pointed end. acting as gunpoint.
36: - the spawnpoint area is calculated as the sum of all the tiles per player(2 tiles per player). converted into a rectangle where the length and breadth have least difference.

1: # commieD — Agent Notes
2: 
3: ## Scope
4: - This repository contains the ghost minigames and the main-game prototype.
5:   The minigames are self-contained modules; the main game is in `main-game/`.
6: - Minigames:
7:   - Soul Clicker (Soul Contribution / HP clicker)
8:   - Bullet Press
9:   - Stewed Luck (power-up spin)
10:   - Dash Supplement Factory
11: - `minigames.md` holds the working specs, pseudocode notes, and unresolved questions. Read it before implementing.
12: - `idea.md` is the product source of truth. Never edit it.
13: - `checklist.md` tracks verified minigame and main-game work. Add only real tasks and tick items only after verification.
14: 
15: ## Current state
16: - The minigames are self-contained; there is no root `package.json` or shared tooling. Each uses vanilla ES modules + `node --test`.
17: - Soul Clicker, Bullet Press, and Dash Supplement Factory are implemented. Stewed Luck is not started.
18: - The main game is a local browser prototype in `main-game/`: deterministic three-pass maze, shared team HP/ammo/dash, movement, combat, special items, ghosts, revival, elimination, winner detection, bots, and HUD.
19: - Authoritative multiplayer networking, city sharding, and lobby are not built yet.
20: - The `.py` files and `dash supplement factory` notes are user-written draft pseudocode, not production implementations.
21: 
22: ## Integration contract
23: - Build each minigame as a self-contained module with a narrow interface: explicit inputs/state in, resources/events out.
24: - The host game integrates minigame modules through explicit resource contributions; minigames do not own the main loop, networking, or global game state.
25: - Keep game logic deterministic and testable; avoid wall-clock time inside rules.
26: - Use placeholder assets until real assets arrive, and keep asset paths centralized.
27: - The main-game core (`main-game/src/game.js`) is deterministic; rendering, input, and networking stay outside it.
28: 
29: ## Minigame rules to follow
30: - **Soul Clicker:** at 5 CPS generate +1 HP/s, banked until needed; below 5 CPS lose 0.2 HP/s. No HP cap for teams with ghosts. Normal team regen is disabled while ghosts exist. HP bar is red below `100 × living teammates`, yellow through `+90`, green above. Random shapes spawn every 10–30 s for a small HP bonus.
31: - **Bullet Press:** players follow keyboard sequences to make magazines. Imperfect magazines are rejected and the sequence restarts. Mistakes drop the production multiplier toward 0.5x; a long clean streak raises it slowly to 5x.
32: - **Stewed Luck:** live-player kills earn killmit; spend it to spin the pot for a special power-up.
33: - **Dash Supplement Factory:** follow the pot-preparation order exactly; any mistake destroys the whole batch. 1 pot = 20 seconds of speed, 1 bottle = 1 second.
34: 
35: ## Rules
36: - One small step at a time; do not scaffold the whole system at once.
37: - Commit after each completed step; never include unrelated or user changes.
38: - Test as you go, with only the minimal tooling a minigame needs.
39: - Do not reintroduce ghost shooting.
40: - Update `checklist.md` at the end of each request when work is completed.
